brief: NVDA's Jensen Huang investigation (NVDA -4.5%) was the tipping point in last week's AI selloff, but washed-out positioning and record Panic Index readings flipped the market into a short squeeze: the Dow, S&P and Russell erased post-election losses as UBS's pre-called asymmetric-upside setup (Nov 5 capitulation, low hedge-fund/systematic positioning) played out, and Goldman, Morgan Stanley and RBC all flag the correction nearing its final phase, though Goldman's Coppersmith still sees large near-term tails and more positioning to work through. Separately, Trump signaling no appetite for extensive Iran strikes plus IAEA-inspector-return rumors sent WTI to six-week lows (-4%, $85 handle) and Brent back to last week's lows, aided by midterm pressure on Washington for an off-ramp. That same risk-on shift pulled capital out of Treasuries instead of into them, lifting yields across the curve (short end worst) on sticky NY Fed inflation data and hawkish Fedspeak from Goolsbee and Barkin. Credit held up despite heavy AI bond supply (ORCL, META, AAPL), even as chipmaker CDS now trades wider than hyperscalers'. Bloomberg's Monkam warns the probe itself could inject lasting governance and key-person risk given NVDA's ~25% share of SPX variance.
